### What does this PR do?

> **Draft — not intended for merge yet.** This PR adds the detailed design specification for separate_async fault tolerance, as the review surface for a community discussion. It is a design document only: no code is introduced or changed. Tracking RFC: #8380 — the design update and discussion live in that issue.

The spec describes the **v2 recovery-source scheme**: per-step engine-native snapshot → local staging → aggregated FT store, with the trainer side and the rollout side each self-recovering from the store, independently and without disturbing each other.

Key design points:

- **Snapshot data plane**: end-of-step engine-native save (one shape for both FSDP and Megatron) → local staging (keep-2, seconds) → async FT shipper → aggregated store where `seal` is the single atomic commit point; per-step snapshot (K=1) is near-zero cost at 30-minute-step scale (measured 272 MB/s mean bandwidth).
- **Trainer-side recovery**: full-group in-place restart with rank-aligned reads of staging/store shard files; RPO = 0 at K=1.
- **Rollout-side recovery**: engine-process replacement (building on the merged standalone replica lifecycle APIs) + cold start from the store's canonical θ (HF safetensors; TP re-sharding done by the engine itself).
- **Fail-closed everywhere**: any uncertainty falls back to verl's current behavior (crash + checkpoint restart) — FT is never worse than no FT.
- **FT module**: fault sensing / orchestration / recovery primitives with registration points; 5 thin host integration points; trainer kernels untouched; `trainer.ft.enabled=false` means zero behavior change.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here:
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+state%3Aopen+fault+tolerance
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+state%3Aopen+separate_async+fault
  - No open PR adds this design. The in-flight "dynamic NCCL re-rendezvous + in-memory failover" PR (#7910, first hit of the query above) is convergent implementation work in a different direction — the spec discusses its relationship in the related-work notes; it is not a duplicate and coordination is planned during implementation.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)
  - Module `doc`, type `feat`.

### Test

- Documentation-only change; no code paths affected. Verification done on the document itself: section structure matches the source specification end to end; all four diagrams are Mermaid and syntactically valid for GitHub rendering; no residual CJK text remains in the English translation.

### API and Usage Example

- Not applicable — no API change in this PR. The spec proposes a future `trainer.ft.*` configuration surface (§6.4 of the document), sketched only.

### Design & Code Changes

- Adds `design/separate_async_ft_design.md` (single markdown file, no binary assets; the runtime view is rendered as a Mermaid flowchart with an edge-color legend).
- Open question for the discussion: the final resting place of this document — keep a `design/` directory for RFC-stage documents, or relocate into `docs/` once the design converges. Happy to move it either way.

### Checklist Before Submitting

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Please check all the following items before requesting a review, otherwise the reviewer might deprioritize this PR for review.

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): not run in the authoring environment — the configured hooks (ruff / mypy / config autogen / docs time-info) target Python sources and the `docs/` tree, while this PR touches a single markdown file outside both. Will run before converting from draft if maintainers prefer.
- [x] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs): this PR is itself a documentation addition; integration into `docs/` is the open question above.
- [ ] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover all the code. If not feasible, explain why: no code is introduced — design document only; implementation PRs (sketched as PR-1/2/3 in §5.4) will carry their own tests.
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in [the `ci-request` channel](https://verl-project.slack.com/archives/C091TCESWB1) in [the `verl` Slack workspace](https://join.slack.com/t/verl-project/shared_invite/zt-3855yhg8g-CTkqXu~hKojPCmo7k_yXTQ). files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,606 @@ +# verl Fault Tolerance (FT) — Design Specification + +> **Status — draft for discussion.** Detailed design of the separate_async fault-tolerance proposal, **v2 recovery-source scheme**: per-step engine-native snapshot → local staging → aggregated FT store; the trainer side and the rollout side each self-recover from the store, independently and without disturbing each other. This scheme supersedes the "mutual HA / reverse weight pull" design in the original RFC body; the tracking issue will be refreshed separately once this draft settles. The runtime view in §4 is rendered as a Mermaid diagram; a polished standalone figure may be added later. + +## 1. Background & Goals + +### 1.1 The problem + +Long-run stability is a key pain point of RL training jobs: + +- **#6583**: a 256×H200 production run died after 6 hours when a single vLLM EngineCore process died — the whole job was lost; +- verl's only exit path for process-level faults = **crash the whole job + restart from an on-disk checkpoint** (5–10 minutes, K steps of progress lost) — no relauncher, no max_restarts (#1314, in the maintainer's words: "Currently it just throw the exception and fails, relying on checkpoints to resume training"); +- Faults are not rare, and most are soft: an Llama 3 production run saw 466 interruptions in 54 days; ByteRobust's three-month study found **22.7% of faults recover with a plain hardware restart** — soft faults such as OOM and process crashes dominate, and their recovery cost should be low; +- **#8186 (26Q4 roadmap)** already set two goals: "Trainer restart without interrupting rollout" and "Rollout replica restart without interrupting trainer". + +### 1.2 Structural advantages of separate_async + +The proposal rests on three structural advantages of post-training (RL) over pretraining: + +| Advantage | Pretraining's constraint | separate_async's free replacement | +|---|---|---| +| Soft RL state | Training data is non-regenerable; once lost, it must be re-collected | Rollouts can be regenerated, batches redone, off-policy tolerated → **progress may be lost, correctness is not** | +| Slow, long steps | Second-scale continuous steps make snapshots expensive | Measured ~30-min steps for a 35B run → **per-step snapshot (K=1) at near-zero cost** (mean bandwidth 272 MB/s) | +| Existing dual-engine plumbing | Weight-format conversion / sharded saves are built per stack | `per_tensor_param` enumeration + engine-native save = ready-made contracts at both ends of the snapshot pipeline | + +Moreover, the two sides' fault domains are naturally independent (async decoupling): when one side fails, the other keeps working — "mutual non-interruption" is a constructive result, not luck. + +### 1.3 Goals + +| # | Capability | Acceptance test | +|---|---|---| +| **G1** | Trainer-side independent restart: OOM / process crash / transient hang → same-node recovery in ≤ x min, rollout uninterrupted throughout, version continuity, in-flight batches redone with zero loss | kill -9 / CUDA OOM injection | +| **G2** | Rollout-side independent restart: engine fault → replace + canonical cold start (~2-min scale), trainer not restarted, zero cooperation required | EngineCore SIGKILL injection | + +Three further design goals run throughout: +**G3 universal extensibility** (GPU/NPU × NCCL/HCCL × FSDP/Megatron × vLLM/SGLang — one framework + registrable instances) +**G4 low overhead** (near-zero steady-state impact; zero FT GPU-memory footprint) +**G5 unattended operation** (detect → recover fully automatically; automatic degradation on uncertainty). + +--- + +## 2. Failure scenarios & scope of this phase + +### 2.1 Failure classes (ordered by detection difficulty) + +| # | Class | Topology | Detection outlet | Disposition path | Design depth | +|---|---|---|---|---|---| +| F1 | OOM (memory-side, hardware intact) | unchanged | immediate error — fails loudly, seconds | in-place revival | **core of this phase** | +| F2 | process crash / transient comm hang | unchanged | Ray death notification within seconds; hangs converted to death notifications by probes / bounded timeouts | same as above | **core of this phase** | +| F3 | single-GPU fault (GPU/HBM/NVLink) | changed (card-level) | ECC / health check / driver errors | scale-down re-sharding / pause for repair | skeleton | +| F4 | whole-node death / reboot (incl. rack-level) | changed (node-level and above) | Ray node death notification (GCS) | remote re-assembly (store tier) | skeleton | +| F5 | slow / gray failures (alive but degraded) | half-changed | tail latency / heartbeat jitter (no death notification) | detection + alerting → future disposition | skeleton (detection first) | + +The full eight failure classes (incl. preemption / partition / SDC) converge onto ~2.5 recovery paths: **in-place revival / remote re-assembly / detection-only** — pluggable detection, convergent recovery paths: this is the foundation that makes a unified FT framework viable. + +### 2.2 Scope of this phase + +**Precisely: F1/F2 ∧ node alive ∧ physical topology unchanged ∧ software version unchanged** — "fails loudly + same cards, same nodes, same shape + same code, same config": + +| # | Scenario | Actions per side | +|---|---|---| +| 1 | Transient OOM (trainer-side allocator; engine-domain OOM = #8168 replacement unit) | trainer full-group in-place restart (§5.2) / engine replace (§5.1) | +| 2 | Process crash (kill -9 / segfault / CUDA error / NCCL transient break) | same as above (validated by V1 / R1 / R6) | +| 3 | Transient comm hang / poisoned group handle (alive but unresponsive) | detection conversion (probe / bounded timeout on first sync → forced kill → death notification) → same as above (R7 validates the fallback chain) | + +### 2.3 Out-of-scope scenarios (fail-closed, automatic fallback to current behavior) + +1. **Permanent topology deformation** (scale-down to N-1 / node removal / heterogeneous replacement): trainer-side world-size change = shard re-partitioning, Phase 2; rollout-side replica removal is nearly ready — a low-cost Phase-2 candidate; +2. **Software version change**: the FT automatic pipeline's contract = same version (Ray respawn reuses the same runtime_env); cross-version changes go through verl's existing planned disk-checkpoint resume; +3. **Gray failures (F5)**: v1 provides signal bits + alerting only — detection first (Phase 3). + +Any uncertain situation **fail-closes** to verl's current behavior (crash + manual checkpoint restart) — **FT is never worse than no FT**. Repeated OOM (flapping) is guarded by a restart-budget circuit breaker: the automatic pipeline does not retry indefinitely. + +### 2.4 Disposition tiers + +| Tier | Name | Trigger precondition | Automation | +|---|---|---|---| +| P1 | in-place restart (fast path) | same shape · now ∧ same version | fully automatic | +| P2 | snapshot-rollback restart | same ∧ local staging unavailable (node dead) | fully automatic | +| P3 | degraded operation (scale-down / remote re-assembly) | permanent deformation | Phase 2 | +| P4 | cold start (checkpoint resume) | fallback tier = verl's existing capability | manual (fail-closed baseline) | +| P5 | human intervention | hardware repair / incompatible upgrade / topology rearrangement | manual | + +--- + +## 3. State analysis + +**Runtime state layout**: + +```mermaid +flowchart TB + DRV["Driver — head/login node · TaskRunnerV1 Ray actor · CPU-only
version ledger: step count · weight version N · commit point | replay buffer · in-flight bookkeeping · RNG · dataloader
agent loop manager"] + + subgraph TRN["Training nodes"] + direction TB + THBM["GPU HBM — trainer rank × per-card shard
θ shard · m/v shard | gradients / activations — transient within a step; dies with the process"] + TRAM["CPU RAM — π_old copy — process heap; dies with the process"] + THBM -->|"D2H mirror — on_step_end · stays on-node"| TRAM + end + + subgraph INF["Inference nodes"] + direction TB + IHBM["GPU HBM — EngineCore × per card
θ_TP shard + KV cache (OOM hot spot)
CE worker × per card — weight-group member · weight-receive copy"] + IRAM["CPU RAM — server actor — vLLM frontend · lightweight, model-free
CE pending bookkeeping — engine restarts, it survives"] + IHBM -->|"vLLM frontend/backend"| IRAM + end + + G["Static weight comm group
members = trainer ranks + CE workers
— pure channel · stores no data"] + + DISK[("Disk snapshot
@N-K: model + optim + extra")] + + DRV <-->|"train batch ↓ | loss/metrics ↑"| TRN + DRV <-->|"prompt dispatch ↓ | trajectory return ↑ — bypasses the training side"| INF + + TRN ==>|"update_weights"| G + INF ==>|"delivery to EngineCore"| G + + TRN -->|"save_freq"| DISK + + INF ~~~ G + + classDef driverC fill:#3b82f6,stroke:#1e3a5f,color:#ffffff + classDef trainC fill:#a5f3fc,stroke:#0e7490,color:#374151 + classDef inferC fill:#ddd6fe,stroke:#6d28d9,color:#374151 + classDef groupC fill:#d1d5db,stroke:#374151,color:#1f2937 + classDef tmpfsC fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#b45309,color:#374151 + classDef diskC fill:#a7f3d0,stroke:#047857,color:#374151 + + class DRV driverC + class THBM trainC + class TRAM tmpfsC + class G groupC + class IHBM,IRAM inferC + class DISK diskC + + style TRN fill:#06b6d41a,stroke:#06b6d4 + style INF fill:#7c3aed1a,stroke:#7c3aed +``` + +### 3.1 Two-sided independence + +| Dimension | When the trainer side faults | When the rollout side faults | +|---|---|---| +| Fault domain | trainer process group | a single engine process | +| The other side | **zero restarts**; engines serving throughout | **zero restarts**; trainer keeps training | +| Production during recovery | rollout keeps generating; the buffer absorbs (bounded clock pause if the watermark is exceeded) | trainer keeps training; the remaining replicas carry inference throughput | +| Recovery source | local staging → FT store | FT store canonical θ | +| Disturbs the other side? | no — no disturbance, no waiting, no liveness dependency | no | + +### 3.2 Trainer-side state (11 items) + +| # | State item | Steady-state location | Disposition | Recovery source / mechanism | +|---|---|---|---|---| +| 1 | Parameters θ (shards) | trainer GPU | **recover** | (1) local staging @N — same node, seconds; (2) FT store sealed @N(-1) — cross-node, ~7 min @10GbE; rank-aligned read + manifest layout check | +| 2 | Optimizer (m, v, t) | trainer GPU | **recover** | same as θ — same source, same seal; K=1 ⇒ exact resume from @N | +| 3 | Gradients / activations / unfinished forward | trainer GPU | recompute | the driver **redoes** in-flight batches — semantically identical to pre-fault, zero data loss | +| 4 | RNG state | in-process | not lost | deterministically re-derived by the driver from seed + step (+ backup inside extra) | +| 5 | Global step / version ledger / FT generation | driver | not lost | held authoritatively by the driver | +| 6 | Buffer / in-flight batch bookkeeping | driver | not lost | **buffer retained, not flushed** — with K=1 exact resume, data validity is identical to the no-fault case | +| 7 | LR scheduler | in-process | rebuild | loaded from ckpt extra + fast-forwarded to the current step (ms) | +| 8 | π_old CPU copy | process heap | recompute | automatically rebuilt next round (it exists only for π_old stability, not as a recovery source) | +| 9 | CUDA context / comm handles | in-process | rebuild | new-process init + new rendezvous — process-private state, physically non-inheritable | +| 10 | Local staging / FT store snapshots | node NVMe / independent fault domain | not lost | they survive process death; node alive ⇒ staging is present | +| 11 | CE-worker-side state — pending / weight-group handles | rollout side | not lost | pending preserved; old-generation handles replaced by the G+1 rebuild | + +### 3.3 Rollout-side state (10 items) + +| # | State item | Steady-state location | Disposition | Recovery source / mechanism | +|---|---|---|---|---| +| 1 | Engine parameters θ | EngineCore GPU | **recover** | **cold start from the FT store canonical θ directory** — HF safetensors; TP re-sharding done by the engine itself, 1–2 min; fallback = trainer re-push via the CE worker (#8168 `next_weight_sync`) | +| 2 | KV cache | EngineCore GPU | recompute | re-prefill; async clients continue from the token prefix — already-generated tokens are not re-sampled | +| 3 | In-flight requests / partial trajectories | engine process | replay | client-side bounded replay (regular clients replay the whole turn / async clients continue the prefix) | +| 4 | Sampling randomness state | engine process | rebuild | new engine process — inside the replay path | +| 5 | Pending-request bookkeeping | CE worker | not lost | it survives engine restart (slow path: CE itself dies → bounded-replay fallback) | +| 6 | GPU resource pools / memory quota | held by CE worker | not lost | the new engine takes over the same quota — the basis of "same-pool, seconds-scale" reuse | +| 7 | server_adapter binding | CE worker | rebuild | rebind to the new engine process | +| 8 | Weight-group handles | CE worker | rebuild / skip | provably skippable — see the four-condition predicate in §5.3 — or G+1 rebuild | +| 9 | All state of the other replicas | other replicas | not lost | replicas are isolated; Reliability analysis: critical windows & weight staleness + +### 7.1 Critical windows (recovery risk and guards) + +The governing principle is **degrade rather than gamble**: any window whose state cannot be proven complete and consistent is guarded as a scenario limitation with a fallback — never recover into a known-bad state. + +| # | Critical window | Risk | Guard & fallback | +|---|---|---|---| +| 1 | trainer crashes while a weight sync is in flight | CE workers stuck mid-collective; handles poisoned | CE-side async error handling + bounded watchdog (60–120 s) → abort → destroy; weight group G+1 (V3) | +| 2 | an engine dies while a weight sync is in flight | the engine holds a mixed θ(V)/θ(V+1) state | version-commit protocol — a replica's version advances atomically only after all shards are applied and verified; recovery reads only the store canonical — no intermediate state is readable (R3) | +| 3 | crash mid-snapshot-save / mid-ship | a half-written snapshot read by mistake | **seal atomicity**: an incomplete session file set is never sealed → recovery automatically falls back to the previous sealed (N-1) (V5) | +| 4 | crash mid-disk-checkpoint-save | a half-written checkpoint directory read by mistake | existing manifest atomic-commit semantics; readers only ever see completed checkpoints (V4) | +| 5 | a second fault during recovery itself | recovery code is not a safe zone | idempotent, re-entrant primitives (generation fencing supports this natively); one-shot degradation to the bottom, bounded retries, then fail-closed (V8 / V9) | +| 6 | re-attach ordering after a replica restart | traffic hits a half-ready replica if it re-attaches before passing the health check | strict ordering: inject → health check → re-attach last; generation fencing rejects stale-generation registration | +| 7 | simultaneous / cascading faults on both sides | both sides' state suspect at once | **the two sides' recovery sources do not overlap ⇒ independent parallel recovery** — each pulls from the store, neither waits for the other; a direct dividend of the snapshot scheme (V6 / V7) | +| 8 | the hybrid-switching window | the switching state machine is not idempotent | v1 gate: a trainer fault inside the window fails closed | + +### 7.2 Weight-staleness handling + +**Version model**: trainer head T ≥ completed-sync watermark W ≥ per-replica V_i; store sealed ∈ {N, N-1} (keep-2). In async mode the two sides — and individual replicas — are naturally skewed by up to the sync interval; the recovery design treats this skew as part of consistency rather than assuming both sides are at the same version: + +- **The recovery point is anchored to the snapshot, aligned by construction**: θ and m/v come from the same seal (manifest consistency) — no mismatch is possible; K=1 ⇒ recovery point = the last completed step N before the crash, **RPO = 0**. +- **The seal-lag window (~3%: 60-s flush / 1800-s step)**: a crash mid-ship ⇒ sealed on disk = N-1 while engines are at N — after recovery the engines are one step ahead of the trainer: in-flight trajectories are tagged with the engines' actual version, and the next update_weights does a **full push (no delta dependency — version skipping is safe)** and converges naturally, within the off-policy tolerance async already has. +- **The replay buffer is retained, not flushed**: with K=1 exact resume, the buffer's data-to-θ_N version relationship is exactly what it would have been without the crash (separate_async's buffer routinely holds several steps of version spread) — data validity is unchanged, and refill time is saved. +- **Post-recovery reseed**: the first update_weights fully re-pushes at the recovered version (monotonic version counter, content rolled back); skew stays within async's existing staleness tolerance. +- **update_weights fault tolerance**: a single CE death must not block the trainer's sync loop — dispatch is already registered `ONE_TO_ALL + blocking=False` (structurally friendly); Ray's error propagation for dead actors to be measured in practice, with skip/retry to complete. +- **Safety asymmetry (a rule hard-wired into the framework)**: parameters have no "reset" fallback (parameter reset = random re-initialization = the policy is scrapped) — the store's keep-2 is parameters' last landing; no path may leave parameters without a landing; optimizer reset remains only as a research position. + +--- + +## 8. version protocol correct | +| R6 | CE worker SIGKILL (same-card collateral) | slow path: same-pool respawn + forced G+1 + bounded replay of pending | +| R7 | poisoned group wrongly skipped (faulty-skip tolerance) | bounded timeout on first sync detects it within minutes → converted to the universal G+1 path | + +vLLM and SGLang each run R1–R3 (SGLang with equivalent injections per its process model). + +### 8.2 Acceptance scenarios + +- **G1**: under V1 / V2 injection, trainer recovery ≤ x min; rollout zero restarts and zero interruption throughout; version continuity; in-flight batch redo with zero data loss. +- **G2**: under R1 injection, end-to-end metrics met; trainer zero restarts, no deadlocks throughout. +- **Regression baseline**: with `ft.enabled=false`, all existing tests stay green (zero behavior change); existing separate_async E2E callers remain compatible.
